messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT - SLO breach detected: p99 streaming latency = 7.8s (SLO 2s) for route /v1/generate on dedicated-usw2-pool-17. Queue depth spiked to 320 and warmup success rate dropped to 18%. Paging on-call. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-warmup

Maria G: seeing it too, p95 at 1.4s but p99 blown out. Streaming stalls reported by a handful of customers.

Raj P: @Maria G can you paste the autoscaler logs? want to see handshake times and slot provisioning delays.

Maria G: logs (tail):
```
2026-03-15T02:34:01Z autoscaler: desired=48 provisioned=32 pending=16
2026-03-15T02:34:05Z warmup: success=3 fail=13 mean_time=18.9s
2026-03-15T02:34:12Z queue: depth=295 inflight=120
2026-03-15T02:34:30Z handshake: timeout=10.2s pool=dedicated-usw2-pool-17
```

Kevin L: Warmup is the culprit. We're losing time waiting for model shards to get ready. Seeing KV-cache cold-path storms too.

Samira: customer impact -- CS flagged 2 customers with streaming sessions stalled; both are on mid-tier Dedicated contracts. They're seeing repeated reconnects.

Product - Theo: flagged to me by CS. Any chance of a graceful fallback to smaller model or hosted pool to reduce customer pain?

Oncall SRE: I'm taking primary. Quick mitigation plan: 1) throttle low-priority routes (start with /v1/embeddings-batch) 2) enable immediate fallback to compatible hosted variant for high-traffic customers 3) bump reserved pool by +8 GPUs if capacity available 4) enable aggressive KV-cache retention for active prefixes.

Raj P: I ran a quick check on pool inventory, there are 10 spare slots in adjacent pool (dedicated-usw2-pool-19) but they are configured for a different ABI. Need handshake mapping to allow cross-pool placement.

Jing (Platform): I can open cross-pool placement policy and map ABI -> compatible quantized variant. Rolling policy change would take ~70s to propagate. If we do now we can divert new allocations to pool-19.

Maria G: doing a manual route throttle now: `curl -X POST https://ops-api.local/throttle -d '{"route":"/v1/embeddings-batch","limit":20}'` -> accepted. Expect queue depth to drop a bit in 10-20s.

ops-bot: THROTTLE: route /v1/embeddings-batch limit=20 set by Maria G at 2026-03-15T02:36:11Z :white_check_mark:

Oncall SRE: enabling hosted fallback for customers with high error rates. `route-policy apply --route /v1/generate --fallback hosted-compat-v1 --selector customer_id in (cust-A,cust-B)`

Kevin L: started increasing reserved pool by +8; note billing spike. API call: `infractl allocate --pool dedicated-usw2-pool-17 --count 8` -> allocation pending, handshake times show improvement for new slots.

Samira: CS update sent to affected customers, offering failover to hosted and ETA ~12m for mitigation. They asked for status updates every 10m.

Maria G: metrics: after throttle and fallback enabled p99 dropped from 7.8s -> 2.9s, queue depth down to 140. Still above target but much better.

Product - Theo: good. Do we know why autoscaler didn't provision early?

Raj P: early evidence: autoscaler uses demand predictor trained on sequence-length distribution; sudden burst from a partner running long-context sessions (8x normal tokens) caused underestimation of slot needs. Also warmup pipeline has a serial step that blocks many in-parallel handshakes due to a mutex around KV-cache priming.

Kevin L: submitted a quick hotfix to warmup pipeline: parallelize priming and add optimistic cache entry. Patch id: warmup-parallel-132. Rolling to pool-17 now (canary to 2 nodes).

ops-bot: DEPLOY: warmup-parallel-132 -> canary (2 nodes) started by Kevin L at 2026-03-15T02:44:10Z

Maria G: can we also temporarily reduce handshake timeout from 12s -> 5s so failed handshakes fail fast and fallback triggers?

Jing (Platform): I can flip the timeout in feature flag, will do for pool-17 and pool-19. Doing now.

Oncall SRE: rolling changes complete. Observed p99 now at 1.9s, p95 at 0.9s. KV-cache hitrate increased ~32 percentage points on active prefixes. Queue depth stable ~60.

CS - Elena: notified customers: they accepted hosted failover for the two affected accounts, no data loss reported. One customer asked for root-cause timeline for executive summary.

Product - Theo: collect timeline + mitigation + next steps. We need a mitigation-runbook entry: immediate fallback for long-context bursts, throttle low-priority routes, cross-pool fallback mapping, warmup pipeline parallelism.

Raj P: root cause summary: demand predictor underpredicted due to out-of-distribution long-context partner traffic -> rapid queue growth -> autoscaler slow due to handshake serialization in warmup -> increased p99 streaming stalls.

Maria G: final note: cost of mitigation ~8 reserved GPUs + hosted fallback. We'll follow-up with tuned predictor retraining and a permanent warmup fix.

Oncall SRE: handing off to platform and eng-runtime for postmortem. I/O: paging closed for now. If regressions appear ping me. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (paging): 2026-03-15T03:04:25Z - Summary: p99 peak 7.8s -> mitigated to 1.9s. Affected customers: cust-A, cust-B. Actions: throttle low-priority routes, enable hosted fallback, warmup parallelization hotfix, cross-pool mapping.

Maria G: filing follow-up ticket: https://redwood.internal/issues/INC-2026-345 - postmortem + action items.

Product - Theo: assigning owners: predictor retrain -> Raj, wake-up warmup fix -> Kevin, runbook update -> Maria, customer comms + exec summary -> Elena.

Samira: thanks everyone. Great run on the live mitigation.
